title: Zombie Outbreak: 30 Days Trapped on a Cruise Ship (pilot, full)
note: src: pilot:<id> = ../vo, cruise:<id> = ../cruise/vo, new = ./vo. gap = pause before the line (s).
lines: Day one. You're a waiter on a cruise ship. Three thousand passengers. Seven days at sea.
Then every phone on board buzzes at once. Stay in your cabins.
And the captain stops talking... mid-sentence.
On Deck Five, people are walking strangely. Too slowly. And they're coming this way.
Rule number one. Don't run to the lifeboats. Everyone else will.
You go down. To the one place nobody thinks about. The galley.
Food for three weeks. Water for nine days. And one steel door.
Rule number two. Be quiet. They follow sound.
You push a cart against the door... and you wait.
That night, the engines stop. The lights stay on. Nobody tells you why.
Day three. You learn the ship's new rhythm.
Footsteps above you at noon. Something dragging at midnight. And long, long silences in between.
You ration everything. One can a day. Half a bottle of water. And a mark on the wall for every day you're still here.
Day five. Someone has been in the cold room.
Half your bread is gone. And the infected don't close doors behind them.
Day seven. You wait in the dark to see who's stealing your food.
A flashlight. Orange coveralls. And on the floor... something they dropped.
Whoever it is... knows this ship better than you do.
Day nine. The last bottle of water.
The nearest water is the ice machine in the crew mess. Forty steps down a dark corridor.
Unfortunately, the ice machine is the loudest thing on this ship.
On the way out, you grab one more thing. The lifeboat radio.
Forty steps there. Forty steps back. The last twenty at a full sprint.
This is the Coast Guard on channel sixteen. All ports are closed. Any vessel carrying infected will not be allowed to reach the coast. We will use force.
That night, the speakers in the ceiling click on.
Nobody speaks. Someone is just... listening. Then they click off.
Day twelve. Through the porthole... a light. A lighthouse. The ship has drifted toward land.
Then, deep below you... the engines start again.
And the ship turns away from land.
Someone else is alive on this ship. And they don't want to be rescued.
You could stay in the galley. Safe. Fed. And blind.
Or you could find out who's driving.
The hatch in the cold room opens onto a service tunnel. Two hundred feet of steel. No lights.
Halfway down, you stop. Something behind you stops too.
You wind the kitchen timer... and slide it into a side duct.
Rule number two works both ways.
Don't move. Hands where I can see them. Both of them.
You're the waiter. The one who hums when he's scared.
Turns out you weren't as quiet as you thought.
Day one, the bridge ordered all stop. Then the line went dead. Nobody's opened that door since.
Then the Coast Guard started sinking ships. So every time we drift too close to land... I start the engines and take us back out.
So that's who's driving. Not a ghost. A very tired engineer.
My shift ended at eight a.m. on day one. I just never clocked out.
I can keep us away from the coast. I can't keep us fed.
Two survivors. One kitchen. One engine room.
She keeps the ship alive. You keep her fed.
Day seventeen. You finally ask her about the speakers. The click. The breathing.
Only one place on this ship can open the PA. The bridge.
It has its own water tank. The captain's pantry. Enough for one person... for a month.
One person. Thirty days. You decide not to think about that.
Day twenty. A gray ship on the horizon.
Coast Guard. Kill the lights. All of them.
Unidentified vessel, you are inside a closed zone. Turn around, or we will open fire.
For one long hour, a ship the size of a small town pretends it isn't there.
Then Rosa turns it around. Again.
Day twenty-four. The timer in the duct stopped ringing a long time ago.
And the thing that followed it... just found the way out.
Sound brought it here. Sound can take it somewhere else.
One frying pan. One empty storeroom. One very loud dinner bell.
Day twenty-six. She teaches you the engines. You teach her that canned peaches count as dessert.
Day twenty-nine. Fuel for one more day.
Tomorrow we pick a direction. And we don't come back.
Steering just switched to the bridge. Nobody's been up there in thirty days.
Engine room. This is the bridge.
Thank you for keeping us alive. I'll take it from here.
Thirty days. You survived the outbreak, the hunger and the sea.
You found out who was driving. Now you just have to find out where he's taking you.
